text_blocks.snippet: Seminoma is a type of testicular cancer that originates from germ cells in the testicles. It is a malignant tumor, but generally has a high cure rate, especially when diagnosed early. Seminomas are known to be sensitive to radiation therapy and respond well to treatment.
snippet_highlighted_words: a type of testicular cancer that originates from germ cells in the testicles

list.title: Germ Cell Origin:
list.snippet: Seminomas arise from the germ cells in the testicles, which are responsible for producing sperm.

list.title: Malignant but Treatable:
list.snippet: While seminomas are cancerous, they are often curable with appropriate treatment, particularly when detected in early stages.

list.title: Sensitivity to Radiation:
list.snippet: Seminomas are known to be highly responsive to radiation therapy, making it a key treatment option.

list.title: Age of Onset:
list.snippet: The average age of diagnosis for seminoma is generally between 35 and 50 years old, which is slightly older than other types of testicular cancer.
